# Java Microbenchmark Harness (JMH) Counter Benchmark

Say that we want to implement a thread-safe counter. How would we go about it?
There are different options:

- `synchronized`
- `Lock`
- `AtomicInteger`
- `VarHandle`

Which option has the lowest overhead?

We can use the
[Java Microbenchmark Harness (JMH)](https://github.com/openjdk/jmh) to compare
the four implementations. This benchmark measures the cost of calling
`increment()` and `decrement()` without thread contention; it does not prove
which implementation is best for every concurrent application.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Build the application

Build the benchmark before running it.

```shell
./mvnw clean package
```

(*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and the dependencies were
copied.

```shell
tree --sort=name './target/libs'
```

There should be one application JAR file and its dependencies.

```
./target/libs
├── commons-math3-3.6.1.jar
├── jmh-concurrency-benchmark-1.0.0.jar
├── jmh-core-1.37.jar
└── jopt-simple-5.0.4.jar

1 directory, 4 files
```

## Run the benchmark

1. Run the benchmark.

   Benchmarks require time to complete. The following command takes
   approximately 15 minutes to run. By default, this JMH benchmark uses one
   worker thread, so the numbers compare uncontended synchronization overhead.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path 'target/libs/*' \
     org.openjdk.jmh.Main \
     demo.CounterBenchmark
   ```

   This prints the final JMH summary table. Smaller `Score` values are faster
   for this average-time benchmark.

   ```
   Benchmark                              Mode  Cnt  Score   Error  Units
   CounterBenchmark.testCounterAtomic     avgt   10  2.105 ± 0.008  ns/op
   CounterBenchmark.testCounterLock       avgt   10  4.301 ± 0.005  ns/op
   CounterBenchmark.testCounterSync       avgt   10  5.500 ± 0.005  ns/op
   CounterBenchmark.testCounterVarHandle  avgt   10  2.104 ± 0.002  ns/op
   ```

   In this run, the `CounterAtomic` and `CounterVarHandle` variants are the
   fastest, while the `CounterSync` variant is the slowest. Treat this as a
   result for this benchmark configuration, JDK, and machine rather than a
   universal rule.
